messages:
hana: Heads-up  release pipeline stopped because release-stamp refused to proceed. CI found a regendiff but also found no changelog entry. The weird part: the diff is purely generated type reordering and a tweak to an autogenerated comment.

release-bot: CI: release/sample-monorepo #833 failed  regendiff detected: packages/sample-client/src/gen/types.ts; changelog check failed: CHANGELOG.md missing entry for this version.

pip: pasted diff from regendiff: 
```
- /** Generated by @redwood/codegen v3.6.2 */
- export type Account = { id: string; email?: string }
+ /** Generated by @redwood/codegen v3.6.3 */
+ export type Account = { email?: string; id: string }
```
hana: So two things changed: codegen version bump (3.6.2 -> 3.6.3) and ordering-only reformat. release-stamp is treating both as a regendiff + missing changelog, but product expects a changelog entry only for user-facing API or behavioural changes. This is noisy.

dwight: we hit this before. Options: (A) update release-stamp to ignore generator-only ordering diffs and autogenerated version bumps, (B) require generated-version bumps to have a changelog entry but provide a special "auto-generated" changelog category that doesn't require product approval, (C) prevent codegen minor/patch bumps from influencing generated file headers.

pip: immediate unblock: we can either revert the generated commit so the stamp proceeds, or add a changelog note like "chore: regen generated types (non-functional)" to pass the check. For speed I'd prefer a tiny changelog entry and then open RFC for release-stamp behavior.

hana: I'd rather not litter the changelog with noise every time codegen updates. If we go with adding an "auto: generated" section that release-stamp accepts automatically, that still clutters history but it's scoped. Long-term we need a rule: only diffs that change exported types shape/behavior should require changelog entries. Ordering-only or header-only diffs should be allowed without manual changelog entries.

release-bot: Note: current release-stamp policy: any regendiff triggers changelog requirement. See infra/release-stamp/README.md.

pip: quick PR opened to unblock: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-monorepo/pull/833  adds changelog entry "chore(gen): regen with codegen 3.6.3 (non-functional)" and pins @redwood/codegen to 3.6.3 in the workspace. Also added scripts/regen-verify.sh which runs regen twice to detect nondeterminism.

dwight: that unblocks the cut but we should not rely on manual chores forever. I'll start an RFC: "release-stamp: ignore generator-only ordering diffs" and propose a small heuristic: if all file diffs match regexes for generated file paths and the diffs are only reorders/whitespace/header changes, treat as no-op for semver and changelog. We'll include an allowlist for generated paths and a clause requiring additional checks if codegen version changed.

product-lead: product POV: we don't want accidental behavioral changes bypassing changelogs. Any automation that suppresses changelog requirements must be conservative. If codegen version changed, product should be notified and a brief line in changelog could be OK (auto-generated) so release notes show transparency. But I agree we shouldn't flood changelogs with meaningless noise.

hana: agreed. RFC should include guardrails: a) require that generated-only diffs are validated by a regen-idempotency job, b) if codegen version bump is detected, run a compatibility test suite (sample-apps + core integration tests) automatically before skipping changelog enforcement, c) keep an audit log of suppressed changelog events.

pip: added automated compatibility suite to the PR so the change runs sample-app smoke tests after regen. If tests pass and diffs are ordering-only, the release pipeline will be able to proceed without a manual changelog entry.

dwight: filing RFC INF-2110 and assigning owners: eng-infra for release-stamp, eng-ml for deterministic codegen patches, devex for regen-idempotency tests.

product-lead: I will review RFC once drafted. We need to balance dev velocity and customer-facing transparency.

hana: merging the PR unblocks this particular release. Thanks everyone. Let's treat the RFC as blocking for next month's stable policy change.

release-bot: CI passed for PR #833; merge completed. Release pipeline retried and publish succeeded. sample-client v0.12.0 published.

pip: leaving a follow-up ticket to retroactively label a few recent regen-only commits as "auto-gen" in changelog for audit purposes.

dwight: noted. Closing thread once RFC is up.
